title: By the clock
rule: Every panel shows the clock, and the time between panels is a constant ten seconds, 4:09:20 to 4:10:30.
declares: keeps E0-E5, the four lines and the outcome
made: page 01's eight panels recomposed from films/swarm/99-ways-template/page/rest/P1..P8 (P5's own clock layers left out and re-laid), c1 balloons as on page 01

the Rothstein clock case (FORAGED, 99-ways-template cutout, white scissor margin) pinned into every panel on a stretch of office wall, its own hour and minute hands re-set on the arbor to each panel's time
a HANDMADE seconds hand (inked needle with counterweight, red) on every clock, at 20, 30, 40, 50, 0, 10, 20, 30 s
a HANDMADE cut-paper time slip under each clock, the time pencilled in red in the shared pen hand (4:09:20 ... 4:10:30)
hand-ruled borders; folio '48 / By the clock' (pen99.folio)

self_check.check: A reader reads a time in every panel, rising by equal steps (structurally verified from the build; legibility of slips and dials judged by the maker from the full-size page; blind reading pending)
self_check.evidence: structurally verified (times set by code) and perceptually judged (full-size page) by the maker

weaknesses: the clock is one wall clock pinned into eight different views, so in P4 and P6 it sits on the ticket-window glass and in P3/P7/P8 on whatever wall the view shows: geography is sacrificed to the rule
the time slips state the time that the dials also show; the seconds hand alone would be hard to read at phone width
a 0.5 px softening of the whole page was needed to bring the JPEG under 1.2 MB
as on page 01 the stranger is never seen; her lines come through the window from off-panel
